messages:

Subject: Follow-up: data isolation questions from today's call

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the call this morning — really helpful overview. A few follow-ups from my side so we can align internally on deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC):

- For Dedicated capacity: can you confirm whether customer data (input prompts + generated outputs) are written to any shared storage outside our tenant? Who has access to instance-level logs and can Redwood SREs access logs for debugging? 
- For Private VPC/on-prem: is the control plane fully customer-managed or does Redwood maintain a managed control plane with VPC peering? What networking artifacts (BGP, VPN, transit) are required for the on-prem option? 
- KMS/HSM: do you support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for both Dedicated and Private? Any limitations on HSM integration?
- Audit logs and evidence: we need to produce artifacts for an upcoming SOC2 scoping call. What's included in the Private deployment audit surface (access logs, kube-level events, operator actions)?

Can you send a short one-pager summarizing the differences and a sample network diagram? That would help our infra and security folks. We're targeting a procurement decision in ~3-4 weeks; a technical deep-dive next week would be great.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Turner
Head of Platform Engineering
FinSecure

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finsecure.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: data isolation questions from today's call

Hi Alex — great to talk earlier. Quick recap and answers to your bullets below, plus next steps.

Recap / short answers:
- Dedicated: customer workload runs in a tenant-dedicated GPU pool; data-in-flight and at-rest are isolated per-tenant. We do not route customer prompts/outputs to shared public buckets, but operational logs (instance-level metrics) are accessible to Redwood SREs for debugging; access is role-based and audited. We can redact prompt contents from those logs on request.
- Private VPC/on-prem: gives you full network isolation. For the Private control plane option, the control plane is managed by Redwood but runs in a customer-owned VPC via VPC peering (or an optional air-gapped on-prem package where you manage everything). On-prem deployment is available for enterprise customers with strict isolation needs.
- KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed keys for both Dedicated and Private. HSM integration is supported for the on-prem/private package; for hosted Dedicated we offer BYOK with cloud KMS integrations.
- Audit logs: Private deployments include application-level audit logs, operator actions, and optional forwarding of OS-level audit logs to your SIEM. We'll provide a SOC2 evidence pack for deployment review.

I've attached a one-pager and an RFI responses template to start (see attachments). Next steps:
1) I'll loop in our solutions engineer (Dylan) for a technical deep-dive — proposed times next week?
2) Please confirm expected concurrency / throughput for sizing (tokens/sec, peak sessions).
3) If you can share target procurement timeline we'll align the quote and SOW.

Thanks — sending Dylan in a separate note with the network diagram and more details.

Best,
Marissa Cole

From: dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finsecure.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-05T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: data isolation questions from today's call — network & KMS details

Hi Alex — looping in a few technical clarifications from the infra side.

On Dedicated vs Private networking:
- Dedicated: workloads live in a tenant-specific project; we expose a private interface and can support VPC peering or private endpoint connections. Traffic between your VPC and the Dedicated cluster goes over the peered network; no public egress for prompts/outputs unless configured.
- Private VPC (managed control plane): we can deploy the control plane into your VPC (managed by Redwood operators with limited access) or provide an on-prem operator bundle. For on-prem, you handle networking (VPN/BGP) and supply the required NAT/egress rules.

KMS/HSM and key handling:
- BYOK supported for both modes. For cloud KMS we integrate with AWS KMS/GCP KMS/Azure Key Vault. For HSM, we support PKCS#11-compatible modules for the on-prem package; for managed Private we can integrate with your cloud HSM with a dedicated key material path.
- We never store plaintext prompts in long-term storage. Customer keys are required for encryption at rest and for rotating keys; we can provide key rotation logs for audits.

Logs / access:
- Audit trail includes: API request logs (can be forwarded to your SIEM), operator action logs, infra-level events. We can provide temporary RBAC for Redwood SREs for incident response; all such actions are logged and we can provide attestations for SOC2.

See attached network diagram (Network_Architecture.png) showing peering vs control-plane-in-VPC options.

If you can share expected peak TPS and retention requirements (how long you need logs kept), we can size Dedicated pools and propose caching/quantization to reduce cost.

Thanks,
Dylan
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Network_Architecture.png
